content: Melting is a physical process in which a substance transitions from a solid state to a liquid state. This occurs when the internal energy of the solid increases, typically through the application of heat, until it reaches a specific temperature known as the melting point. At this temperature, the solid undergoes a phase change into the liquid state. A substance that has completely melted is referred to as molten. The melting point of a substance is a fundamental characteristic property. However, the melting point is not always identical to the freezing point, as demonstrated by the phenomenon of supercooling. For instance, in the case of water, the formation of ice crystals often requires a nucleation site, such as a seed particle. On a very clean glass surface, water can remain in a supercooled state, several degrees below its melting point, without freezing. In fact, fine emulsions of pure water have been observed to cool to as low as -38 degrees Celsius without ice nucleation occurring. This distinction highlights that while the melting point is a definitive property of a substance, the freezing point is not. When the internal energy of a gas is increased by an external energy source, the molecular vibrations within the substance intensify. As these vibrations increase, the substance becomes progressively more ordered. This process is also referred to as fusion. Substances melt at a constant temperature, which is their melting point. Even with the continued application of energy, the temperature does not increase further until the substance has completely transitioned into the molten state. From a thermodynamic perspective, at the melting point, the change in Gibbs free energy (ΔG) of the material is zero. This is because both the enthalpy (H) and entropy (S) of the material increase during melting (ΔH, ΔS > 0). The melting process occurs when the Gibbs free energy of the liquid phase becomes lower than that of the solid phase for the given material. This transition happens at a specific temperature for a given pressure. Furthermore, it can be mathematically expressed as ΔS = ΔH / T, where T represents the temperature at the melting point, ΔS is the change in entropy during melting, and ΔH is the change in enthalpy during melting.
